Yes. Hansen Global Forest Change data detected a **candidate tree-cover loss of 13.5 hectares in 2025**, about 3.9% of the property.

The finding is **pending corroboration** because 2025 is the latest year in the series; a later observation is needed to assess persistence. The detection does not establish the cause, whether deforestation or land-use change occurred, or whether the activity was legal.
